blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how banks calculate the interest on your savings or loans? Let's explore how simple and compound interest work!

blocks.markdown: In commercial arithmetic, interest is the cost of borrowing money or the reward for saving. There are two main types of interest: simple interest and compound interest.

blocks.title: Simple Interest
blocks.text: Simple interest is calculated using the formula $I = \frac{PRT}{100}$, where $P$ is the principal, $R$ is the rate, and $T$ is the time in years.

blocks.markdown: Compound interest, on the other hand, is calculated on the initial principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods. The formula for compound interest is $A = P(1 + \frac{r}{100})^n$, where $A$ is the amount, $P$ is the principal, $r$ is the rate, and $n$ is the number of years.

blocks.title: Compound Interest Formula
blocks.text: Remember that compound interest grows faster than simple interest because it is calculated on the accumulated amount.
